sentence_stem: By the time the train arrives,
correct_completion: we will have been waiting here for two hours.
full_sentence: By the time the train arrives, we will have been waiting here for two hours.
acceptable_variants: we will have been standing on this platform for hours.
we will have been sitting on this bench all afternoon.

options.text: we wait here for two hours.
options.why_wrong: The simple present does not express the duration up to a future point that the time clause sets. The future perfect continuous is needed.

options.text: we waited here for two hours.
options.why_wrong: The simple past refers to a finished past period and does not fit a future time clause with 'by the time'.

options.text: we will have been waiting here for two hours.
we have been waiting here since noon.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect continuous looks at the present and past, not at a point in the future, so it conflicts with 'by the time' plus a future clause.

grammar_focus: Future perfect continuous with 'by the time' clauses
explanation: With 'by the time', the main clause uses a future tense to describe an activity that will still be in progress at a future moment. Portuguese speakers often use a simple future here, because Portuguese has an equivalent future form but learners may not map the continuous aspect onto it.
translation: Quando o trem chegar, teremos esperado aqui por duas horas.
